sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: cAMP EC50 and maximum response to agonist: unchanged vs. untagged receptor (L2). Ligand-binding affinity (Ki): unchanged vs. untagged receptor (L3). Surface expression confirmed by live-cell HA immunostaining in HEK293 cells (L4).
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly names the junction as Ala17–Glu18 in CRHR2α. Python search of the canonical sequence finds Ala at position 17 (matching) but Leu at position 18 (not Glu); the sole Ala→Glu junction near the N-terminus is canonical 19–20, the SP cleavage site, implying a 2-residue shorter SP in the α-isoform used. Inserting after canonical residue 19 places the tag at the very start of the 95-residue extracellular N-terminal domain (20–114), well clear of TM1 (begins at 115). Functional assays (cAMP, binding) and surface labelling all confirm tolerance. Full-length HA-tagged human CRHR2α expressed in HEK293 cells; HA inserted between the paper's Ala17 and Glu18 (described as 'an inert region of the amino-terminus'). The only Ala→Glu junction near the N-terminus in the canonical sequence is at positions 19–20 (the SP/mature-protein boundary), consistent with CRHR2α carrying a 16-aa signal peptide vs. the 19-aa canonical SP, giving a +2 offset between paper and canonical numbering. Tag is surface-displayed and used for live-cell labelling.

sources.claim: The influenza hemagglutinin (HA) epitope tag (YPYDVPDYA) was inserted between residues Ala 17 and Glu 18 , which is an inert region of the amino-terminus (N-terminus) [ 19 ], using oligo-directed mutagenesis (Quick Change™ kit, Stratagene, La Jolla, CA).
The lack of tools to track the CRH receptors prompted us to use a construction of the CRHR2α with a FLAG tag on the amino terminal to generate stable HT22-CRHR2α clones.

literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) concern the same protein region (extracellular N-terminus of CRHR2α) and reduce to two sites at the same canonical junction (insert_after_residue=19). L2 and L3 provide functional validation for the L1 HA-tag site and are cited in evidence_detail rather than as independent sites. L4 and L6 confirm surface/cellular expression for L1 and L5 respectively. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion or C-terminal tag for CRHR2. The paper's residue numbering (Ala17–Glu18) does not match canonical positions 17–18 (Ala–Leu); Python analysis identifies canonical 19–20 (Ala–Glu) as the only Ala→Glu junction near the N-terminus, consistent with CRHR2α having a 2-residue shorter signal peptide than the canonical β-isoform sequence. The tag at insert_after_residue=19 sits within the cleaved SP in canonical numbering but is extracellular in the expressed protein because it is placed after the actual SP cleavage site of the α-isoform.
